title: Understanding the Surprising Generalization Properties of Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.17957v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) increasingly rely on in-context learning, where a model receives labelled examples at inference time and predicts labels for new inputs without updating its weights. Existing TFMs are typically trained on either massive synthetic corpora or very large collections of real datasets. In contrast, we show that surprisingly strong transfer can emerge from self-supervised pre-training on just a single real table. In this setting, we also find that tables tend to be either broadly useful or broadly poor regardless of downstream prediction task, and that the strongest predictor of usefulness is the number of features rather than the number of instances. This leads to a task-centric interpretation of tabular pre-training: the number and the quality of tasks are essential for the pre-training of TFMs.   We show that the same task-centric perspective can help corpus design at scale: fine-grained column-level pre-pro

translated_title: 理解表格基础模型惊人泛化特性的研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17957v1 公告类型：新 摘要：表格基础模型（TFMs）越来越依赖于上下文学习，即模型在推理时接收带标签的示例，并在不更新权重的情况下为新输入预测标签。现有的TFMs通常在大型合成语料库或非常大的真实数据集集合上进行训练。相比之下，我们表明，仅在单个真实表格上进行自监督预训练，就能产生惊人的强大迁移能力。在这种设置下，我们还发现，无论下游预测任务如何，表格往往要么广泛有用，要么广泛无用，而最有用的预测指标是特征数量，而非实例数量。这导致了对表格预训练的任务中心解释：任务的数量和质量对TFMs的预训练至关重要。我们表明，同样的任务中心视角可以帮助大规模语料库设计：细粒度的列级预训练。
tldr: 本文发现仅用单个真实表格进行自监督预训练即可产生强迁移能力，且表格的有用性主要取决于特征数量而非实例数量，从而提出任务中心视角的表格预训练理论。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that self-supervised pre-training on a single real table can yield surprisingly strong transfer, with table usefulness primarily determined by feature count rather than instance count, leading to a task-centric interpretation of tabular pre-training.
